recognize_zh: 細胞核分葉、染色質粗，細胞質中僅剩少數深紫色粗顆粒，其餘多為淡色空洞樣區域，是嗜鹼性顆粒在染色時被水洗脫（washed-out granules）的嗜鹼性球。
features: Granulocyte slightly larger than adjacent red cells
Lobated nucleus with condensed, dark chromatin, now clearly visible
Cytoplasm with residual scattered coarse dark purple granules
Numerous pale, empty-appearing vacuole-like spaces where granules have dissolved
A small platelet at the upper left of the cell; background normochromic red cells
describe_en: High-power peripheral blood smear shows a granulocyte with a lobated nucleus with condensed chromatin. The cytoplasm contains a reduced number of coarse dark purple granules and numerous pale, empty-appearing spaces, giving a vacuolated appearance. Because the granules are diminished, the nucleus is more visible than in a typical basophil. Findings are consistent with a basophil with water-soluble granules partially washed out during staining, an artifact rather than true dysplastic degranulation.

ddx.vs: Toxic neutrophils have pale pink cytoplasm with fine toxic granules and discrete vacuoles, not residual coarse purple-black basophilic granules.
Morphology may overlap; true dysplasia is persistent across well-stained smears and accompanied by other dysplastic changes, whereas washout is technical.
Mast cells have a round non-lobated nucleus and densely packed uniform granules that are not water soluble.
